NDT training in Vancouver: how it works for Vancouver employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT runs ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Lower Mainland employers and technicians. We teach it live online or onsite at your shop, yard or plant, under ASNT Level III oversight. We have no classroom in Vancouver. Canada's national scheme is still CAN/CGSB-48.9712, certified by NRCan's NDTCB. Our training suits Vancouver companies that work to US codes or for US clients, including jobs across the border in Washington State.

Vancouver's NDT market works under two certification systems. Most Canadian owners, including pipeline operators, the Burnaby refinery, LNG projects, provincial utilities and many fabricators, expect technicians to hold certification from Natural Resources Canada's National Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body (NRCan NDTCB), issued under CAN/CGSB-48.9712. That is the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712. It is a central scheme, so the technician holds the certificate personally and keeps it when they change employers.

An hour south of the Peace Arch crossing is a different system. Whatcom and Skagit counties in Washington State have refineries at Cherry Point, Ferndale and Anacortes. There is aerospace manufacturing around Everett and Renton, and naval and commercial shipyards on Puget Sound. Most of these employers qualify NDT people under ASNT's SNT-TC-1A. That is an employer-based system: the company's written practice sets the rules, and a Level III examines and certifies each technician.

Atlantis NDT trains to SNT-TC-1A. We don't claim CGSB or NDTCB recognition, and our courses do not replace NDTCB certification where a BC owner requires it. Here is where we fit:

  • Lower Mainland contractors and fabricators with US clients. Firms that inspect or fabricate for Washington refineries, US-owned plants, or US buyers of ASME-code vessels and piping.
  • Firms supplying US-code projects. For example, modules, skids and spools built in BC for US installation, where the purchase order calls for SNT-TC-1A-qualified NDT personnel.
  • Companies with no full-time Level III. Firms that need an outside ASNT Level III for written practices, procedures, exams and certification sign-off.
  • Technicians who want strong method theory. For example, UT, PAUT and TOFD fundamentals are the same physics under every scheme, although exams and hour credits depend on the scheme you certify under.

If that fits your company, request a Vancouver training quote with your methods, levels, head count and preferred delivery.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Vancouver

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. We deliver it to Vancouver cohorts live online, onsite, or as a mix of the two. Your written practice sets the exact training hours, experience, and exam content. For the reference figures, see our NDT training requirements matrix rather than relying on numbers quoted secondhand.

MethodLevelsWhat Vancouver employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepHull and structural weld inspection at shipyards, thickness surveys on terminal and refinery piping, weld inspection on fabricated vesselsLevel I: basic maths and reading. Level II: Level I plus the experience in your written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection on pipeline and plant piping, corrosion mapping, alternative to RT on new construction where specifications allowConventional UT, normally Level II
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section welds on vessels, cryogenic and LNG-related fabrication, crack sizingConventional UT, normally Level II
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds, process piping, castings and valves, marine piping systemsRadiation safety training and CNSC operator credentials for gamma sources, in addition to method training
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepSurface cracks on ship structure, cranes and lifting gear at the port, structural steel, mining-equipment componentsNone for Level I. Level II needs Level I plus experience
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and aluminium welds, cryogenic piping, non-magnetic marine and aerospace partsNone for Level I. Level II needs Level I plus experience
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual acceptance on structural and marine work, fit-up and hold-point inspection, remote visual inspectionNone for Level I. Adequate near vision
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepHeat exchanger tubing at the refinery and industrial plants, surface cracks on coated structures, aircraft component inspectionNone for Level I. Level II needs Level I plus experience

UT. The course runs from sound-wave fundamentals and calibration to angle-beam weld inspection, DAC and TCG, and evaluation against acceptance criteria. Much Lower Mainland UT work is structural and marine rather than process piping, so we adjust the specimens and code examples to your job mix. That could be ASME Section V and VIII, AWS D1.1 and CSA W59, or a class-society rule set.

PAUT and TOFD. These courses cover probe and wedge selection, focal laws, scan planning, encoded data capture and analysis. TOFD adds diffraction theory and height sizing. BC has been building pipelines, marine terminals and LNG facilities, and that work has made encoded, recordable UT a sought-after skill in the province.

RT. The course covers radiation physics, exposure technique, film and digital imaging, image quality indicators, and interpretation of weld radiographs. It does not give anyone the right to operate a gamma camera. For that, see the licensing FAQ below.

MT, PT and VT. These are the daily methods of shipyard, structural and port-maintenance work. Level II training concentrates on technique choice, telling relevant indications from non-relevant ones, and clean, defensible reports.

ET. Covers impedance-plane theory, probe selection, reference standards, and applications from exchanger tubing to surface-crack detection on aircraft and marine components.

Candidates preparing for the ASNT Level III examinations can use our ASNT Level III training for the Basic exam and method exams.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Vancouver, step by step

The SNT-TC-1A route is the same for a technician in Burnaby, Surrey or Bellingham. This is the order:

  1. The employer adopts a written practice. The written practice sets the rules for training, experience, exams, vision tests, certification and recertification by method and level. If your company doesn't have one, our written practice development service can build it with you.
  2. Formal training. The technician completes the classroom hours the written practice requires for the method and level, delivered live online or onsite. The training requirements matrix lists the usual reference hours.
  3. On-the-job experience. The technician builds supervised, documented experience in the method. Shipyard, fabrication or plant work counts if it is logged to the written practice.
  4. General examination. A written test on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on the employer's procedures, equipment, and applicable codes, for example ASME Section V, AWS D1.1, API 1104 or a client specification.
  6. Practical examination. The technician inspects real specimens with known flaws, then records and evaluates the results. An NDT Level III administers or oversees the exam.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity each year, and colour contrast as the written practice requires.
  8. Employer certification. The employer certifies the technician in writing and keeps the records: training, experience, exam grades and vision results.
  9. Recertification. At the interval set by the written practice. A change of employer normally means certifying again under the new employer's practice.

Remember that SNT-TC-1A certification stays with the employer that issued it, while NDTCB certification stays with the technician. For the full picture, read our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Vancouver crews

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Vancouver or anywhere else in British Columbia. We work in two ways:

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory taught in real time, with questions, worked problems and quizzes. This suits the Lower Mainland's spread-out workforce, from the North Shore to the Fraser Valley. It also suits crews working away at Kitimat, Squamish or interior sites who can't come back to town for a classroom block. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. An Atlantis instructor delivers training and practicals in your shop, yard or plant, on your equipment and on specimens matching your work: plate and pipe welds, marine structural joints, exchanger tubing or castings. For multi-method or multi-site programmes, see corporate NDT training.

Scheduling around your work. Lower Mainland NDT demand comes in peaks: refinery and terminal turnarounds, vessel refits and drydock windows, and construction milestones on pipeline and LNG projects. We plan cohorts backwards from those peaks, so theory is done before a refit or turnaround starts and the practicals and exams fall in a quieter period. Send us your calendar and you will have a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

To plan it now, ask about onsite training for your Vancouver crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Vancouver

Metro Vancouver's NDT work is spread across more industries than most Canadian cities:

  • Shipbuilding and ship repair. Seaspan's Vancouver Shipyards in North Vancouver build federal vessels under Canada's National Shipbuilding Strategy. Several yards and drydocks along the Burrard Inlet and Fraser River handle repair and refit. Marine NDT works to class-society rules and owner specifications, with heavy use of VT, MT, UT and RT on hull and piping welds.
  • Refining and fuels. The Burnaby refinery on Burrard Inlet is the Lower Mainland's only refinery. It needs corrosion monitoring, piping and vessel inspection, and turnaround campaigns.
  • Pipelines and marine terminals. The Trans Mountain system ends at the Burnaby Terminal and the Westridge Marine Terminal. The expansion added large amounts of new pipe, tanks and dock infrastructure that now need in-service inspection. Federally regulated pipelines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator, provincially regulated ones under the BC Energy Regulator. Most pipeline welding and inspection work follows CSA Z662.
  • LNG. FortisBC's Tilbury LNG facility is in Delta, and Woodfibre LNG is being built near Squamish. Vancouver is also the main contracting and fabrication base for LNG Canada at Kitimat. Cryogenic stainless and nickel-steel welds make PT, UT, PAUT and RT important here.
  • Port, cranes and bulk terminals. The Port of Vancouver is Canada's largest port. Its container cranes, bulk loaders, conveyors and mooring structures need routine MT, UT and VT on structural welds and lifting equipment.
  • Aviation. Airline and business-aviation maintenance around YVR, floatplane operators, and component shops in the Fraser Valley all use ET, PT, UT and VT. Aerospace employers usually qualify personnel to NAS 410 or EN 4179. We mention that as context only, because Atlantis does not train to those standards.
  • Utilities, forestry and mining services. These include hydroelectric penstocks and turbine components, pulp-mill digesters and recovery boilers, and Vancouver-based engineering firms supporting mines across the province.
  • Washington State. Cherry Point and Ferndale near Bellingham, and the two Anacortes refineries, are within commuting range for turnaround work. So are Puget Sound's shipyards and aerospace plants. Almost all of these employers work to SNT-TC-1A.

Codes you will meet locally. Boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping in BC are regulated by Technical Safety BC under CSA B51, which references ASME Sections I, V and VIII and B31.1 and B31.3. Pipelines work to CSA Z662. Structural steel works to CSA W59, and welding fabricators are certified by the Canadian Welding Bureau under CSA W47.1. In Washington you will meet AWS D1.1, API 1104 and ASME codes, plus NAVSEA technical publications on naval work.

Radiography licensing. In Canada, the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) licenses companies that own and use gamma exposure devices. It also certifies the individual exposure device operators. Industrial X-ray use falls under WorkSafeBC's occupational health and safety requirements. In Washington, an NRC Agreement State, the state Department of Health licenses radioactive-materials radiography, and industrial radiographers need certification equivalent to the federal 10 CFR Part 34 requirements. A crew working both sides of the border must meet both sets of rules. RT method training is needed as well as these credentials, but it doesn't replace them.

What Vancouver employers typically ask for. On BC projects: NRCan NDTCB certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, often with CWB-related welding inspection credentials on the quality team and owner-specific qualifications. For US-client and Washington work: SNT-TC-1A certification backed by an auditable written practice. Many Lower Mainland firms end up maintaining both.

Level III services and written practices for Vancouver NDT companies

For many Vancouver firms, the most valuable thing Atlantis offers is ASNT Level III support. The typical case is a BC inspection or fabrication company with NDTCB-certified technicians that is winning US-code or Washington State work. It needs to stand up an SNT-TC-1A programme that will pass a US client's audit. That usually means:

  • A written practice built for your methods and clients. It should match the current SNT-TC-1A edition and any client or code additions, for example ASME Section V requirements or an owner's specification. Our written practice development service writes it with you.
  • Outside Level III services. Administering and grading exams, reviewing experience records, and signing certifications under your written practice, for companies without a full-time Level III.
  • Procedures and technique sheets written to the code and client specification for each job type.
  • Pre-audit review of certification files, vision records and training logs before a client or owner audit.
  • Guidance on crediting prior NDTCB training and experience. We explain how your written practice can document that history while still examining technicians under SNT-TC-1A. We never promise equivalence. Your written practice and your client make that call.

The SNT-TC-1A certification guide sets out employer responsibilities. If you would rather talk it through, book a Level III consultation for your Vancouver programme.

Practise before the practical exam

Atlantis offers Practical NDT, a 3D simulator where trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site, and a storage tank. For Vancouver trainees, the welding workshop suits shipyard and fabrication work, the aircraft hangar suits aviation maintenance, and the oil and gas site and storage tank match terminal and refinery work. It helps trainees:

  • rehearse calibration and scanning sequences
  • get familiar with indications
  • walk through the steps of an inspection before they face real specimens

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the SNT-TC-1A practical exam, which is performed on real specimens and graded under Level III oversight. It also doesn't count as on-the-job experience. Treat it as preparation, not as a credential.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs the course content, oversees onsite and live-online delivery, and provides Level III oversight of examinations under the employer's written practice. When your Vancouver team trains with Atlantis, you deal directly with the Level III responsible for the programme.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Vancouver

How do I get NDT certified in Vancouver?

First decide which scheme your employer or client needs. Most BC work expects NRCan NDTCB certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, which you apply for through NRCan and test for under its rules. For US-code or US-client work, including Washington State, your employer certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice after training, experience, exams and a vision test. Atlantis delivers the SNT-TC-1A route.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Vancouver employers?

Yes, by employers and clients working to US codes and by nearly all Washington State employers. Many BC owners and projects require NDTCB certification instead or as well. Confirm the requirement with the owner before you pick a route. Atlantis doesn't claim CGSB or NDTCB recognition.

Can I take NDT training online in British Columbia?

Yes, the theory portions run live online with an instructor, so you can join from anywhere in BC, including remote project camps. Practical training and practical exams need real equipment and specimens, and we run them onsite at your employer's facility. See NDT training online.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Vancouver?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Vancouver or any other city. We teach live online and onsite at the employer's shop, yard or plant.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer's written practice sets it. It is a mix of classroom hours for Level I and II plus a set amount of documented on-the-job experience, and the experience usually takes the most time. The reference figures are in our training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in British Columbia?

For gamma radiography, yes. The CNSC licenses the company and certifies individual exposure device operators. X-ray work falls under WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety rules. RT method training is required as well as these credentials, not instead of them. For work in Washington State, that state's radiation programme and US radiographer certification rules apply.

What does NDT training cost in Vancouver?

We quote on request. The price depends on the method, the level, the group size, and whether delivery is live online or onsite. Send your requirements and we will reply with a quote within one business day. Get a Vancouver NDT training quote.

Can you train shipyard or fabrication crews at our facility?

Yes. Onsite delivery is built for that. Practicals use your equipment and specimens that match your welds, and we schedule around refit, drydock and production peaks.

Does Atlantis offer CGSB, ISO 9712, CSWIP or NAS 410 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Vancouver employers also ask for CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ISO 9712, CSWIP, NAS 410 and welding inspector credentials, and those come through other schemes and bodies.

Which NDT method is most useful for a new technician in the Lower Mainland?

VT, MT and PT at Level I are a common start, because shipyard, structural and port work uses them daily. UT follows, and then PAUT and TOFD for pipeline and LNG-related work. For earnings context, see our NDT salary guide.

How do I prepare for a UT Level II exam?

Use our UT Level 2 practice questions, rehearse calibration in the Practical NDT simulator, and build supervised hands-on hours. The practical exam is done on real specimens.

Our company has no Level III. Can Atlantis provide one?

Yes. We provide outside ASNT Level III services: written practices, procedures, exam administration and certification sign-off under your written practice. See written practice development or our full training catalogue.
